questions.q: According to Microsoft's guidance summarized in this lesson, how do CLI v2 and SDK v2 compare?
options: The CLI can only manage compute; the SDK does everything else
There is no difference in functionality; the CLI can suit CI/CD automation while the SDK can suit development
The SDK requires the studio, while the CLI does not
Only the CLI can submit training jobs
questions.explain: Microsoft's docs say CLI v2 and SDK v2 have no difference in functionality; the CLI is often more convenient in CI/CD MLOps scenarios and the SDK for development.

questions.q: Which interface is best suited to a quick, no-code look at a run's metrics, logs and lineage?
options: A hand-written REST call
A YAML file committed to git
The Azure ML studio
A Bicep template
questions.explain: The studio is the place to explore the workspace and inspect finished runs: metrics charts, logs, code snapshots and data lineage.

questions.q: What command submits a YAML job definition with CLI v2?
options: az ml job create --file job.yml
ml_client.jobs.run('job.yml')
az storage blob upload job.yml
python job.yml
questions.explain: CLI v2 commands follow az ml <noun> <verb> <options>; az ml job create --file <yaml> submits a job.

questions.q: Why keep job definitions as YAML files in version control?
options: YAML jobs run faster than SDK jobs
Git automatically fixes bugs in YAML
The studio refuses jobs that were not stored in git
Text definitions can be code-reviewed, so changes to data version, parameters or compute show up clearly in a diff
questions.explain: The lesson's difflib demo shows a two-line change to the data version and n_estimators. Reviewable, versioned configuration is the seed of MLOps.

questions.q: You find an online tutorial that uses azureml-core, Workspace, Experiment and ScriptRunConfig. What should you conclude?
options: It is SDK v2 code and is safe to copy unchanged
It is the legacy SDK v1 style; for new work use SDK v2 (azure-ai-ml) and check the docs' migration guidance
It only works in the studio
It is a CLI v2 tutorial
questions.explain: Those names belong to SDK v1. Microsoft's docs recommend v2 (azure-ai-ml, MLClient, command) and give end-of-support dates for v1.
